isolated Bonefish and D-Bus runtime without donor SquashFS mounting
owned MCU heartbeat independent of WAMP connectivity
owned DSP boot, exact image download, command-response order, and process-level recovery
BlueZ and BlueALSA autonomous startup with readiness ordering
active-PCM lease, ALSA RUNNING, owner-TID, and executable-gated physical mute policy

validation: The predecessor autonomous image booted from RAM in five seconds and started router, MCU, DSP, D-Bus, BlueZ, BlueALSA, playback, pairing, and network services without host staging.
A fresh allowlisted RAM bond completed and a muted five-second A2DP stream advanced ALSA hardware pointers.
MCU process survival and hardware heartbeat continued across a router restart.
The kernel SPI GPIO wait returned ETIMEDOUT instead of leaving an unkillable spidev_sync thread.
The v8 image cold-booted and passed all 20 machine checks plus physical control, pairing, and muted A2DP acceptance.
The v8 guarded audible test produced no sound and exposed I2C arbitration loss plus an over-broad ALSA RUNNING policy.
The corrected v9 runtime, BlueALSA player, MCU and DSP services, and initramfs are byte-for-byte reproducible and pass the complete host and race suites.
The v9 image has not been booted.
safety: Writable raw MTD nodes are removed; only /dev/reinvoke-nand-ro mode 0400 remains.
Automatic physical unmute requires a live BlueALSA PCM-data lease whose worker TID matches both ALSA owner_pid and the expected executable.
GPIO processing requires a real POLLPRI edge before reading the MCU over I2C.
Service logs are bounded by rotating syslog storage with a kernel-ring fallback.
NAND persistence and boot-slot work remain explicitly excluded.
